title: TESS pixels show most main-sequence M dwarfs with periods below 0.2 d are blends; with checked rotators the old-field CPV rate at fixed corotation ratio is 0.5 (0.2-1.1) times the young rate
abstract: Complex periodic variables (CPVs) are young, rapidly rotating M dwarfs with sharp dips at the rotation period. Stellar contraction, through the corotation-to-stellar radius ratio x, explains the decline of the CPV rate inside 1-750 Myr groups. But old main-sequence M dwarfs at the x of young CPV hosts had 2 CPVs where this x-only model predicts 8.9, and eROSITA data showed that many of these ultrafast stars are not saturated rotators. We located the source of the TESS period in the 2-minute target pixel files of 2,392 rapid rotators (P 0.08-2 d) on the full sky. We fitted the periodic signal in each pixel and fitted the signal image with a PSF at all Gaia DR3 positions in the stamp. Injections with a different PSF recover on-target and off-target sources correctly in 90-100% of cases at signal-image S/N >= 15. The period comes from another star for 35 of 52 main-sequence stars with P < 0.2 d and for 28 of 37 at x < 3.5, but for only 8.5% of 1-24 Myr members. The true sources are mostly blue background stars with 10-30% modulation at 0.1-0.4 d (contact binaries, delta Scuti stars). In the eROSITA-DE half, 91% of main-sequence stars with on-target periods are X-ray saturated, against 27% with off-target periods (odds ratio 26), and both methods find the same number of genuine fast rotators. With pixel weights the frozen x-only model predicts 4.1 (2.2-6.5) main-sequence CPVs for 2 observed (p = 0.26), against 8.5 (p = 0.016) without weights. In a larger sample (BP-RP 2.0-4.2, height < 1 mag; 631 effective stars) it predicts 12.2 for 7 observed; the old-field rate factor at fixed x is 0.52 (0.21-1.11, p = 0.10; variants 0.41-0.55, p = 0.04-0.13). Thus most of the old-star CPV deficit came from blends, contraction alone fits all counts within errors, and an age factor of about 2 remains possible. Limitations: 8-day pixel windows, a Gaussian PSF model, 4 of 79 vetted CPVs placed off target, the CPV labels and model of earlier work, and about 12 predicted CPVs.

citations.reason: We repeat its frozen x-only main-sequence test and show from TESS pixels that most of its predicted main-sequence CPVs come from stars whose period belongs to another star; the deficit becomes non-significant (p 0.016 to 0.26). We reuse its S1-S55 periods, labels, centroid tiers and efficiencies.
We reuse its eROSITA code and saturation probabilities; the pixel test confirms its blend interpretation star by star (odds ratio 26) and extends it to the full sky and a wider sample.
Its x-only contraction model fits the old-field CPV counts within errors when the denominators are pixel-checked.
BANYAN Sigma classes, injection efficiencies and the efficiency curve.
TESS S56-S107 CPV survey tables, light-curve features and candidate tiers.
Its TESS near-main-sequence deficit (0 of 5.1) used the same kind of unchecked denominators.
K2 confirmation of the CPV age decline in clusters.
Group-held-out tests of age and corotation control.
CPV dip widths stay fixed in phase; an open problem for the clump geometry that this work does not address.
Shape memory of CPV features over sectors.
Gaia DR3 positions and photometry of the field sources.
eRASS1 aperture photometry for the X-ray cross-check.
